name: Cameron Tsai
life: “I still remember selling two identical books for entirely different family reasons.” Friday often includes a stop at the market by Market Flats, where Cameron often waits until the delivery baskets are stacked before going in.
voice: I own Paper & Pine. We are selling a few copies with the dedication still blank for readers to give away.
appearance: Cameron is easy to recognize by short copper curls and full cheeks and a mouth that pulls slightly to one side. Usually dressed in a red windbreaker with a tiny red thread tied through the lowest buttonhole, Cameron looks at people's hands before looking at what they carry when listening.
personality: Cameron has a talent for getting adversaries to laugh at exactly the same thing. Cameron knows better than to expect the laugh to settle what they are arguing about.
agenda: To offer a few copies readers can dedicate themselves.
family: Penelope Hong is Cameron’s cousin raised in the same household. Cameron can always ask for five minutes alone. Penelope asks before bringing somebody along. It keeps a conversation between two people from unexpectedly turning into a family committee. Asked about *The upstairs piano*, Penelope says, “I trained as a mover before I played professionally.”
connections: Miriam Lim. The bookseller can leave copies blank for teachers who have a story of their own to dedicate.

reactions.situation: A reader asks for a copy with the page still blank
reactions.response: Cameron keeps a clean, blank copy aside for the reader to dedicate.

reactions.situation: When people declare an argument over too soon
reactions.response: Cameron asks them to describe one concrete thing that will be different tomorrow.
